blueprint_topic: Management of Care — client education and care coordination related to liver-transplant allocation and MELD medical urgency
stem: A client on the liver-transplant waiting list asks what the current MELD score means. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: It is a medical-urgency score used to help prioritize most candidates age 12 and older; actual offers still follow OPTN allocation and match-run rules.
options.B: It mainly tracks waiting-list duration, so a longer wait directly raises transplant priority even when medical urgency and match circumstances are unchanged.
options.C: It estimates how well a liver graft is expected to function after transplant and is used mainly to rank candidates by predicted long-term graft survival.
options.D: It is a diagnosis-specific score used chiefly for alcohol-related liver disease, while candidates with other liver diseases are prioritized through separate systems.

rationale: A is correct. Current HRSA/OPTN materials define MELD as a calculated formula used to assign priority to most liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older based on medical urgency. Current liver-allocation materials also show that MELD is part of a broader allocation framework: special status categories, exception scores, and match-run rules can affect how candidates are prioritized for an individual offer. B is incorrect because MELD is not a waiting-time score; waiting time may be used within match-run sorting rules but does not replace medical-urgency scoring. C is incorrect because MELD's allocation role is based on pretransplant medical urgency and wait-list mortality risk, not primarily on prediction of long-term graft survival after transplant. D is incorrect because MELD is used broadly for liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older and is not restricted to alcohol-related liver disease.
educational_objective: Explain that MELD is a current OPTN medical-urgency score used to help prioritize most liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older, while actual organ offers continue to follow the broader OPTN allocation and match-run framework.

source_locator: HRSA/OPTN MELD Calculator — introductory paragraph: MELD is a calculated formula used to assign priority to most liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older based on medical urgency; page also states the current calculator applies to candidates 12 and older. HRSA/OPTN Liver and Intestine — Allocation calculators: MELD and PELD are numerical scales used for liver allocation, with MELD for ages 12 and older. HRSA/OPTN Liver Allocation FAQ — current allocation discussion: candidates with higher MELD/PELD scores generally receive first consideration at each distribution level, while exception scores and broader allocation rules affect ranking and offers. Current policy material also identifies special Status 1A/1B categories and exception-score processes distinct from standard MELD/PELD scoring.
source_claim_supported: Current HRSA/OPTN sources directly support MELD as a medical-urgency priority score for most liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older and show that liver allocation uses a broader policy framework than MELD or waiting time alone, including special status and exception-score pathways and match-run rules.

correction_summary: Rebuilt all four alternatives to remove the original extreme correct-answer length cue and the 'solely/only' distractor pattern. The final choices test realistic misconceptions about waiting time, post-transplant graft-survival prediction, and diagnosis-specific use while preserving one concise medical-urgency/allocation explanation. Post-fetch adversarial reread found no further defect requiring another rewrite.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects HRSA/OPTN's definition of MELD as a medical-urgency priority score for most liver candidates age 12 and older while avoiding the false claim that MELD alone determines every offer.
option_audit.B: Plausible waiting-time confusion; incorrect because MELD is based on medical urgency rather than elapsed waiting time, even though waiting time can appear in match-run sorting rules.
option_audit.C: Plausible outcome-prediction confusion; incorrect because the allocation role of MELD is pretransplant medical urgency/wait-list mortality risk, not primarily long-term post-transplant graft survival.
option_audit.D: Plausible disease-specific confusion; incorrect because current OPTN materials apply MELD broadly to liver-transplant candidates age 12 and older rather than only one liver-disease etiology.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on solely/only/always/never/all/must-type distractor absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final options are balanced in length and professional detail; A is not uniquely longest and no option is identifiable by an obvious formatting cue.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel explanations of what MELD measures and how it relates to transplant priority.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after post-fetch adversarial reread. B, C, and D each contain a distinct claim contradicted by current HRSA/OPTN materials.
